cutover.heading: Choose your first trip in DiveDay
cutover.intro: Try one representative trip before changing the system your crew relies on.

crewFirst.title: Let the crew walk their screens first
crewFirst.detail: The live demo runs the same roles your dock does. Have the captain run a roll call and the desk see who’s not ready before you move a single record.

step1.title: Choose where each booking is managed
step1.detail: Keep taking bookings in your current system during the trial. If you prepare the same trip in DiveDay, staff create its departure and add the divers; importing history does not book their seats.

step2.title: Check bookings and balances together
step2.detail: Compare upcoming departures, deposits, refunds and outstanding balances before changing your booking link. Keep the original records and receipts.

step3.title: Review changes while both systems run
step3.detail: A contact re-import can update records matched by email. It does not transfer new bookings, cancellations or reschedules automatically. Assign someone to check those changes in both systems.

step4.title: Set the date after your trial
step4.detail: Allow time to correct the file, collect missing documents and let the crew practice. The size and quality of your records determine the work; we review that with you before the move.

cutover.midSeason: You can trial DiveDay mid-season while your current system stays in use. Start with a sample export and one trip, then review the remaining work before choosing a handover date.

contact.detail: Imported as given. A row with an email matches an existing diver on re-import; without one, it is always a new record.

emergencyContact.detail: Name and phone, when your file has them.

diveInsurance.detail: Carried across as free text, exactly as your file holds it. Never a gate, only detail the crew wants on hand.

rentalSizes.detail: BCD, wetsuit, boot, and fin sizes become a rental-fit profile.

certificationCard.detail: Comes across with the diver’s record, marked imported, and clears the level gate unless your file says the card was never verified, in which case it waits for staff. Unrecognized levels need manual entry.

specialtyCards.detail: Marked imported. Each one’s gate stays shut until staff give it a one-tap confirm, whatever your file says.

nitrox.detail: Marked imported. Until staff give it a one-tap confirm, that diver gets plain air. Boarding waits on it only where your file says the card was never verified.

signedWaivers.detail: A row marked already-accepted is trusted, medical clearance included, and marked imported. Individual medical answers are never reconstructed, only the outcome.

waiverDocuments.detail: Fetched once from your file’s URL and kept for audit. Images and PDFs up to 5 MB.

role.detail: Everyone imports as a diver, never a staff role or a login.

cardOnFile.detail: Stay with your payment processor. DiveDay never imports card numbers or CVCs.

pastVisits.detail: One row per booking up to today becomes visit history. It is not a dive, and it never appears on your schedule or counts toward capacity.

paymentHistory.detail: Source payment, refund, and receipt rows come across as unverified history in Orders. A clearly parsed amount in your shop currency is counted in the revenue and refund totals. It never becomes a live Stripe order or booking payment.

serviceHistory.detail: Comes across through the separate gear-history CSV. Units match by tag or serial number, and dated service records stay attached to the right unit.

diverNotes.detail: Customer remarks and staff notes become private notes on the diver’s profile.

eve.cardSummary: Compare the crew’s daily work, while keeping the retail and PADI processes you rely on.
eve.metaDescription: Compare DiveDay’s trip preparation and roll call with your EVE workflow. Review export options, retained records and the work involved before moving.
eve.heroTitle: Bring your regular divers into a better-prepared dive day
eve.heroLede: Keep each diver’s records close to the trip your crew is preparing. Try the morning checks and roll call in DiveDay before deciding what to move from EVE.

context.item1: EVE already handles dive-shop sales, courses and PADI processing. If those are central to your business, test them separately: DiveDay does not replace a retail register or submit certifications to PADI.
context.item2: The reason to try DiveDay is the crew’s daily work: checking missing records before departure, preparing the rental kit and calling every person aboard. Walk those screens with the people who will use them.
context.item3: You choose the files to export. We help review what they contain before you commit to changing systems.

eve.exportHeading: Get your data out of EVE
eve.exportIntro: EVE documents spreadsheet exports for sales. Customer and certification export options depend on your setup; confirm them with EVE support before planning a full move.

step1.title: Confirm which records you can export
step1.detail: Ask EVE support about customer, certification and visit-history exports for the version you use. Keep access to EVE until you have checked the files.

step2.title: Keep an original copy
step2.detail: Save each file unchanged. If it arrives as an Excel workbook, make a CSV copy for the DiveDay preview.

step3.title: Check a few returning divers
step3.detail: Look for their names, contact details and certification numbers. Check whether history and certifications need separate files or manual matching.

step4.title: Preview the sample with us
step4.detail: The preview identifies recognized columns and rejected rows. Resolve any missing fields before exporting the rest.

exportNotes.note1: These are preparation steps, not a verified menu path for every EVE version.
exportNotes.note2: Keep retail records and original documents even if they are not part of your DiveDay import.
exportNotes.note3: Historical visits do not create future departures or bookings. Prepare those departures separately with your crew.

diveshop360.cardSummary: Keep the retail tools you need. Compare trip preparation, diver readiness and the crew’s roll call.
diveshop360.metaDescription: Compare DiveDay with your DiveShop360 workflow. See the dive-day tools, what your retail shop would still need, and how to review customer and certification exports.
diveshop360.heroTitle: Give the crew a clear view of the next departure
diveshop360.heroLede: See who still needs a waiver or a certification check, prepare their gear and run roll call from the boat. Compare that work in DiveDay before replacing any part of DiveShop360.

context.item1: DiveShop360 combines retail sales with dive-shop tools, including rentals, servicing and courses. Keep it if its register, inventory and vendor workflows are doing work you need. DiveDay is not a retail POS replacement.
context.item2: Try DiveDay if you want trip preparation organized around each diver: the missing record, the kit to pack and the next roll-call checkpoint. The demo lets your crew judge that fit before an import.
context.item3: DiveShop360’s FAQ lists customer, inventory, sales and certification exports. Review the actual files with us; the published list does not establish the columns your account will provide.

diveshop360.exportHeading: Get your data out of DiveShop360
diveshop360.exportIntro: Start with customer and certification exports. DiveShop360 confirms those datasets are exportable; ask its support for the current steps and file format for your account.

step1.title: Confirm the export options for your account
step1.detail: Use DiveShop360’s help or support to find the customer and certification exports. We do not need access to your account.

step2.title: Save the customer file
step2.detail: Check the selected date range and filters, including inactive customers you want to keep. Keep an unchanged copy of the export.

step3.title: Inspect the certification file
step3.detail: Check which fields connect a certification to a customer. Do not assume two separate files can be matched without preparation.

step4.title: Preview a representative sample
step4.detail: We help map the columns and check the records before the full import. Convert a copy to CSV if needed.

exportNotes.note1: The FAQ confirms exportable datasets, not a universal click path or file schema.
exportNotes.note2: Keep inventory, sales and original signed documents for your own records, even when they are outside the contact import.
exportNotes.note3: Open repair jobs and future bookings need separate preparation; a contact CSV does not create them.

diveshop360.importerNote: Start with contacts, then review how any certification rows identify the same diver. Imported records remain subject to the checks in the field reference below.

smartwaiver.cardSummary: Bring waiver collection into the booking and trip-preparation workflow while preserving your signed originals.
smartwaiver.metaDescription: Compare Smartwaiver with DiveDay’s booking and trip-preparation workflow. Export participant data, preserve signed PDFs and review what the import can accept.
smartwaiver.heroTitle: Put the missing waiver beside the diver’s next trip
smartwaiver.heroLede: DiveDay connects bookings, release forms and departure checks, so the crew can see whose paperwork still needs attention. Bring your participant records from Smartwaiver after reviewing the signed evidence you need to keep.

context.item1: Smartwaiver is a dedicated waiver service with its own collection and document workflows. Keep it if those workflows or your current integrations are the right fit.
context.item2: Choose DiveDay for the work around the waiver: a diver books, completes the required forms and appears on the crew’s preparation list. An unresolved requirement stays visible before boarding.
context.item3: A participant CSV and the signed waiver PDF are different records. Preserve the originals and review the release version, acceptance and any medical evidence before relying on an imported status. Importing does not establish legal validity or create a new signature.
context.item4: Your existing terms determine when someone needs to sign again. We help map the file; your shop decides which evidence it can rely on.

smartwaiver.exportHeading: Get your data out of Smartwaiver
smartwaiver.exportIntro: Smartwaiver publishes separate instructions for participant data and signed PDFs. Keep both when planning the move.

step1.title: Open Export Data → Participant CSV
step1.detail: In the Smartwaiver dashboard, choose Export Data from the sidebar, then Participant CSV.

step2.title: Choose the records you need
step2.detail: Filter by submission date, waiver title or tag. Check the selection includes the participants and release versions you intend to retain.

step3.title: Select Export Waiver Data
step3.detail: Save the CSV unchanged, then make a copy for the DiveDay preview. Inspect custom fields rather than assuming which details are present.

step4.title: Save the signed PDFs separately
step4.detail: Smartwaiver’s support can arrange a bulk PDF download for a date range. Confirm access and retention before ending your subscription.

exportNotes.note1: Only fields present in your export can be considered for import. Custom questions may need manual mapping.
exportNotes.note2: The preview names the columns it recognizes and those it will ignore. Check both lists before confirming.
exportNotes.note3: Keep the signed originals independently. A CSV acceptance status is not the original signed document.

smartwaiver.importerNote: Review participant identity and any acceptance evidence separately. A CSV does not guarantee that signed PDFs, medical documents or every custom answer will transfer.

fareharbor.cardSummary: Compare the dive-day workflow, and plan what happens to your booking links and distribution.
fareharbor.metaTitle: FareHarbor and DiveDay: run the dive day, or switch
fareharbor.metaDescription: Compare FareHarbor and DiveDay for dive-shop bookings and trip preparation. Review the manual transfer, distribution tradeoffs and records before switching.
fareharbor.heroTitle: Keep the bookings coming. Prepare every diver for the boat
fareharbor.heroLede: If your crew still checks cards, chases forms and builds the boat list outside FareHarbor, try that work in DiveDay. Decide whether to keep your booking channel or take new bookings here after a trial.

context.item1: FareHarbor handles booking and distribution. If its reseller relationships bring you customers, include that value in your decision: DiveDay does not provide an equivalent distribution network.
context.item2: The useful comparison is a real departure. Can your crew find the missing form, check the required certification and account for each diver after the dive? Try those tasks in the demo against the process you use now.
context.item3: Compare your current FareHarbor agreement with DiveDay’s published offer, including payment processing and any distribution charges. Your contract and booking mix determine the cost; this guide does not estimate savings.

coexist.heading: Choose what stays in FareHarbor
coexist.intro: Keep your booking channel while testing DiveDay with one departure, or move new direct bookings after the trial. Either path needs a clear handover for the crew.
coexist.bridgeNote: There is no automatic connection to FareHarbor. CSV imports bring supported contacts and historical records; staff create upcoming departures and seat divers in DiveDay, then check new bookings, changes and cancellations in both places.
coexist.replaceHeading: Take new direct bookings in DiveDay
coexist.replaceBody: Your booking link can open the DiveDay schedule, with payment through your Stripe account. Test the booking and preparation flow, then review outstanding bookings and balances before replacing the link.

website.heading: Check every booking link before changing your website

about.phoneFrameLabel: A captain calling the roll in DiveDay, name by name, one tap on each circle.
about.heroDescription: In January 1998, Tom and Eileen Lonergan went out on a dive boat to St. Crispin’s Reef, on the Great Barrier Reef. The boat went back to port without them, and nobody noticed they were missing until two days later, when their bag turned up still aboard. Neither of them was ever found.
about.heroP2: That story is why we built DiveDay. A head count is a number, and a number can come out right while someone is still in the water, so DiveDay’s roll call names every diver and crew member before the boat leaves and after every dive, and it isn’t finished until each of them is accounted for.
about.peopleTitle: Divers who have shipped software to millions of people
about.peopleP1: The people who build DiveDay have spent their careers on software that millions of people rely on, and their weekends on dive boats. We know the desk from the diver’s side, cert card out while the owner hunts for the waiver, and the deck, where a divemaster works down a wet clipboard while the boat waits. DiveDay is the tool we wanted in both places: records a shop can trust, on a screen a wet thumb can work.
about.peopleP2: The dive shops we know run the day on a whiteboard by the door, a clipboard that goes out on the boat, a spreadsheet somebody updates by hand, and a handful of apps that each keep their own list of the same divers. The owner knows every diver by name, and each morning some of that knowledge gets copied from one tool to the next while the rest rides along in their head. DiveDay is built so that knowledge is written down once and goes out with the boat on the captain’s phone.
about.buildTitle: The one job on a boat that can’t go wrong
about.buildDescription: The roll call is the one record on a dive day that has to be right the first time, so it is where DiveDay starts. The booking, the waiver, the certification check, the gear sizes and the payment each have a screen of their own, and every one of those screens is there so that the captain opens the manifest with the records in order and the only job left is reading the names.

survivesDock.title: The roll call runs with no signal
survivesDock.body: Open DiveDay on a crew phone while there is still signal and it keeps a copy of the manifests for the trips ahead, so the roll call runs from that copy once the harbor is behind you. The buttons are sized for a wet thumb. Spray or a wet palm on the glass lands as several touches at once, and the roll call ignores it.

privacy.title: What we hold, where it lives, and how it leaves
privacy.updated: Describes DiveDay as it works today.
privacy.intro: DiveDay is dive-shop software. Most of the personal data in it belongs neither to us nor to the shop alone: it is the shop’s divers’ data, held on the shop’s instruction. This page says what we hold, who else can touch it, and how it comes back out. It describes current behavior rather than intentions, and where something is still being decided it says so.

roles.heading: Two different relationships
roles.shopBody: we are the software they run their business on. Their staff hold accounts with us, and we hold what they put in.
roles.diverBody: we hold data on the shop’s instruction. A waiver, medical answers and certification evidence are the shop’s records, in the shop’s own tenant. They are not sold or used to train anything, and they never move between shops. A diver wanting to see or delete their record should ask their shop, which can do both from inside DiveDay. DiveDay’s own 30-day copy of AI suggestions sits outside that record, and a diver can ask us to see it.

collect.heading: What is stored
collect.staffBody: a name, an email address, a hashed password, and the shop and role the account belongs to.
collect.diversBody: name, contact details, an emergency contact, certification level and the evidence a shop verifies against, rental sizes, and the bookings they hold.
collect.waiversBody: the signed release and the health questionnaire a shop asks before a dive. This is the most sensitive thing in the system and is treated that way: it renders only to the shop’s own staff and to the diver holding the link, and it never appears in a log line or an analytics event.
collect.paymentsBody: DiveDay never sees a card number. Cards are entered directly with Stripe on the shop’s own connected account. We keep the amount, the state and Stripe’s identifiers, so a shop can reconcile a refund without us holding anything worth stealing.
collect.trailsBody: who moved a booking, who marked a diver aboard, whether a confirmation arrived. Short who-did-what-when rows, in the shop’s own tenant.
collect.textsBody: a mobile number given with a booking is used only to text that diver about their bookings, from DiveDay’s own number. Mobile numbers and the consent to text them are never shared with or sold to anyone for their own marketing. Replying STOP to any text stops them, and the number stays on a stop list so it is not texted again until the diver replies START.
collect.devicesTerm: The copy on a boat phone
collect.devicesBody: So that a roll call still works with no signal, a crew phone holds its own copy of the next two days of manifests. For each diver it keeps their name and emergency contact; their rental sizes and whether they asked for nitrox; who is on their buddy team; whether they checked in or the desk marked them as not coming; whether they are cleared to board and, if not, why, which can be a medical hold; and each roll-call mark, with the name of the crew member who made it and any note they wrote. It is stored encrypted on that phone, under a key the browser will not hand back out, so it cannot be read off the device’s storage. Anyone holding the unlocked phone can open it, the same as the paper manifest it replaces. It is removed when a different shop signs in on that phone, and it deletes itself at the earlier of fourteen days after it was saved or seven days after the trip ended.

where.heading: Where it is processed
where.body: Primarily in the United States. The database is Neon, the application and its file storage run on Vercel, and the mail, messaging, backup and monitoring pieces run in AWS. Vercel serves the site from wherever the reader is, so a request is first answered near them before it reaches the United States.

processors.heading: Who else touches it
processors.intro: Each of these is a service DiveDay runs on, and each sees only the slice it needs:
processors.stripeBody: payments, on the shop’s own connected account. Card details go to Stripe directly and never through us.
processors.awsBody: sending email and SMS, storing the weekly backups, and holding logs and performance metrics.
processors.metaBody: WhatsApp messages, and only for a shop that has connected its own WhatsApp sender. A shop that has not connected one sends Meta nothing.
processors.vercelBody: hosting, the file storage that holds photos and certification evidence, and page-level analytics. Analytics records which pages are viewed; we do not attach a diver’s or a staff member’s identity to a page view.
processors.anthropicBody: Claude, the AI model behind DiveDay’s suggestions, and only for a shop that has them turned on. It receives only what a suggestion needs. Across all of them, that is: messages divers send the shop, with the shop’s earlier replies in the same conversation, and replies staff ask it to draft, sort or translate, with the shop’s schedule, open seats and prices; a booking ask, from an email or a staffer’s note of a phone call; two diver records staff are comparing as a possible duplicate, sent as each one’s name, date of birth, email address before the @, last four phone digits, certification levels and the months the shop first and last saw them; a diver’s own note about the gear they rent; a certification card photo, from staff or from a diver registering with the shop, read and then discarded; the column headers DiveDay could not match, a few masked sample values and the level spellings of a file being imported; the shop’s blank waiver form; the shop’s own website; the text and details the shop wrote for its trips, courses and dive sites; review comments; work-order notes; the words the crew type or dictate about what they saw, with the sightings, sites and conditions they logged; the words a staffer types to search the diver list; and the counts in the shop’s weekly digest. Answers to the medical questionnaire, and the medical alert a diver writes for the crew, are never sent. A message, note or review goes as it was written, so anything a diver chose to put in it goes too. Anthropic processes this only to answer the request, under its commercial terms, does not train its models on it, and deletes it within 30 days, unless a request is flagged under its usage policy. DiveDay keeps its own copy of what was sent and what came back for 30 days, so we can find and fix a suggestion that went wrong. Only DiveDay can read it; the shop cannot, and it is not in the shop’s export. A diver can ask us to see it. When a reply draft finds that a diver asked about their health, the copy of that draft keeps none of the message; another suggestion that read the same message, such as sorting it, keeps it as written. A photo or a PDF itself is never kept, but what the suggestion read off it is, such as a card number or the text of the shop’s blank waiver form. A website’s pages are not kept either, only their addresses. Erasing a diver deletes everything kept for that shop; for anyone else, it goes when its 30 days are up. A copy already in our backups stays there until that backup expires.
processors.sentryBody: error reporting. When something breaks, the crash is sent here so we can fix it. The address of the page is stripped of any token before it goes. Passwords, cookies and form contents are never sent; an error message can mention the booking or diver it was working on.
processors.googleBody: the embedded map on a dive-site briefing and on a diver’s trip-prep page. Opening one of those pages reaches Google directly, so it sees the request the way any embedded map does; the page’s own link is withheld from it.
processors.pushBody: browser push notifications for staff who turn them on. Each gets a device address and an encrypted payload it cannot read.

links.heading: Links that work as keys
links.body: Some of what DiveDay sends is a link that needs no password: the waiver a diver signs, their trip-prep page, the recap after a dive. Holding the link is the permission, so it can be opened on a dock with one hand free. Those links are treated as credentials throughout: the token is removed before a page view is recorded or an error reported, and before any line reaches a log. They expire, and a shop can invalidate one.

extension.heading: The certification-check extension
extension.intro: Shop staff can add DiveDay’s certification check to Chrome or Edge. It does one thing: when a staff member presses “Check with SSI”, or another agency, on a diver’s card in DiveDay, it looks the card up on that agency’s own lookup page, from their browser, and hands the answer back to DiveDay. It runs only then, and only on DiveDay’s staff pages and the agencies’ lookup pages.
extension.sendsTerm: What it sends to the agency
extension.sendsBody: the diver’s name and what that agency’s form asks for, a birth date or a card number, and only to the agency the staff member chose, as typing them in would. For a course student’s PADI eLearning, the student’s email goes to PADI.
extension.readsBody: the agency’s answer. On the PADI Pros’ Site, which a staff member opens under their own shop’s PADI sign-in, it hands back only the lines about that diver, and for a student’s eLearning only the student’s own lines. When a check fails, it may send DiveDay the page’s structure (its labels, button words and headings, never anything typed into it or anyone’s details) so the reader can be fixed.
extension.keepsBody: when the answer shows the card, the agency’s words for it become the card’s review note, with the name of the staff member whose browser checked. When the page lists other cards for the diver and a staff member adds them, the agency’s lines for the diver become those cards’ review notes too. Otherwise nothing from the agency’s page is kept.
extension.neverBody: it holds no password and no agency sign-in, stores nothing in the browser, reads no other site and no browsing history, and passes nothing to anyone for advertising, for sale or to judge credit.

keep.heading: How long it is kept
keep.intro: The shop’s own records are kept while the shop is using DiveDay, and go when the shop deletes them or ends its account. Most append-only trails have fixed windows, and these are the real numbers the system prunes on:
keep.delivery: Message delivery attempts: 400 days. These hold provider identifiers and error codes rather than message bodies, though a provider’s own error text sometimes quotes the address it failed to reach.
keep.bounces: Email that bounced or was marked as spam: 90 days. Each record holds the address, the reason the receiving server gave, which email it was, and who sent it, so we can fix delivery problems.
keep.payments: Payment event history: 7 years, matching the ordinary horizon for financial records. The orders and payments themselves are the shop’s records and stay until the shop removes them.
keep.webhooks: Payment-processor event records: 400 days. These hold no diver data at all.
keep.tokens: Expired sign-in and reset tokens: 90 days past their own expiry. A live one is never pruned.
keep.assists: What an AI suggestion was sent and what it answered: 30 days, and in backups until they expire. Only DiveDay can read it, and a diver can ask us to see it. A photo or a PDF is never kept, only what was read off it.
keep.safety: Roll calls are kept for as long as the shop uses DiveDay, and incident reports for seven years; if a diver asks to be erased, their own record is unlinked from both, and the words staff wrote about the day stay.
keep.history: The record of who changed a departure’s plan, and of who published or hid each review, is kept for as long as the shop uses DiveDay.
keep.reviewBody: how long a signed waiver and its medical answers should be kept after a diver stops diving with a shop. Today they stay until the shop removes them, because a release is evidence a shop may need years later, and shortening that without advice would be the wrong kind of guess. It is under review with the same counsel reviewing the waiver text, and this page will say the answer when there is one.

out.heading: Getting data out, and getting it deleted
out.exportBody: A shop can download its records from DiveDay as one ZIP, from its own settings, on any day, without asking us and without a fee. It is the same bundle our own backups are made of. A few internal tables are left out of it (delivery retry mechanics, device registrations, the sealed credentials for a shop’s own backup destination, and DiveDay’s own 30-day copy of what AI suggestions were sent and answered). That copy is the one left out that can hold a diver’s words, and a diver can ask us to see it.
out.diverCopyBody: A diver may ask a shop for a copy of what it holds about them, and staff can download it from the diver’s own record page as one ZIP: their bookings, certifications, waivers with the medical answers on them, payments, messages and reviews at that shop, never another diver’s.
out.erasureBody: A shop can erase a diver’s record. Where that record reached a payment processor, the erasure is tracked as owed until it is discharged rather than being declared done at our own edge. A customer object DiveDay deletes itself and confirms. An invoice a processor has already issued is a request a person has to file, and the shop can see it sitting there until they do.

contact.heading: Asking us something
contact.body: Write to <email>{address}</email>. If you are a diver rather than a shop, your shop holds your record and can answer faster; if they cannot, we will help them.
contact.operator: DiveDay is operated by {company}, doing business as DiveDay, at {postalAddress}.

open.heading: What this page does not yet say
open.body: DiveDay is in early access and some of this is unsettled: the retention period for waivers and medical answers, and the formal data-processing terms a shop signs. Rather than publish a policy that reads complete and is not, those are named here as open. The rest of the page describes what the code does today, and none of it is a plan.

terms.title: What we owe each other
terms.updated: Describes DiveDay as it works today.
terms.intro: Plain terms for an early-access product: how DiveDay is meant to be used, what we do and do not promise, and what happens when a shop wants to leave.

what.heading: What DiveDay is
what.body: Software a dive shop uses to run bookings, waivers, certification checks, trip prep and boat manifests. It is a tool the shop operates, not a service that operates the shop. Every judgment that matters on a dock (whether a diver is fit to dive, a certification genuine, or a boat ready to sail) stays with the shop’s own staff. DiveDay shows what it has been told, refuses to hide a gap, and does not decide.

account.heading: The shop’s side
account.accurateBody: a manifest is only as good as what was typed into it, and the boat carries what the shop entered.
account.legalTerm: The waiver is the shop’s own instrument
account.legalBody: DiveDay stores and presents the release and the medical questionnaire. It does not supply their wording or vouch for their sufficiency in any jurisdiction.
account.accessBody: not to a shared login. A shop is responsible for who it invites and for removing them when they leave.

payments.heading: Money
payments.body: Divers pay the shop, not us. Card payments run through the shop’s own Stripe account, so the shop’s money never sits with DiveDay and leaving does not mean extracting funds from us. Stripe’s own fees and terms apply to those payments. What DiveDay charges for itself is on the pricing page.

percentPlan.heading: Plans priced as a percentage of recorded collections
percentPlan.intro: These terms apply if your shop’s agreed plan includes a percentage of recorded collections. Your subscription keeps the rate and monthly fee you agreed to.
percentPlan.feeBody: {percent} of the money your shop records as received in DiveDay in a calendar month{hasBase, select, yes {, with a base fee of {base} each month on top} other {}}. The month follows your shop’s own timezone.
percentPlan.countsBody: money your shop records as received in DiveDay by any payment method, including cash and external payments. A deposit counts when recorded received, and only the later balance counts when it arrives. Unpaid bookings, package redemptions and imported history do not count. Packages count once at sale. Separately recorded tips, tax, park fees and other pass-through charges are excluded. Without a separate tax breakdown, the recorded amount counts in full.
percentPlan.refundsBody: a recorded refund or correction reverses the fee on that money at the rate and rounding of its original statement. A later statement applies the credit once. Unused fee credit carries forward in the same currency, and never expires because a month has no collections. A failed refund reverses its credit. Contact us to settle unused credit after cancellation.
percentPlan.statementBody: early in the next month, Settings shows recorded collections, the rate, refund credits, any credit carried forward and the fee separately for each currency. Amounts are never converted or combined across currencies. Automatic billing currently supports USD only; other currencies need an agreed billing setup before any charge. The running estimate is before credits.
percentPlan.whoPaysBody: the shop, never the diver. DiveDay adds nothing to a diver’s price or checkout.
percentPlan.noticeBody: we tell your shop at least 30 days before we change the rate, the base fee or what counts toward the fee.
percentPlan.feeBodyAgreed: The percentage and any monthly base fee agreed for your shop apply to the money your shop records as received in DiveDay in a calendar month. The month follows your shop’s own timezone.

data.heading: Whose data it is
data.body: The shop’s records are the shop’s. We hold them to run the product and for nothing else: they are not sold, not used to train anything, and they stay inside the shop’s own tenant. A shop can download the whole lot as one ZIP from its settings on any day, without asking and without a fee. How it is handled while we hold it is on the privacy page.

availability.heading: What we do not promise
availability.body: This is early access. We are building the track record behind an uptime guarantee. Today, the export works every day and the offline boat manifest keeps roll call running on a phone with no signal, which is the moment dependable access matters most.

acceptable.heading: Using it for what it is for
acceptable.body: Do not use DiveDay to store data a shop has no right to hold, to send messages the recipient did not agree to receive, or to attempt to reach another shop’s tenant. Every shop’s data is isolated, and probing that boundary ends an account.

ending.heading: Ending it
ending.body: A shop can stop whenever it wants. Export first; the button is in settings and needs no conversation with us. We may end an account for the misuse above, or if a shop stops paying, and in either case the export stays available long enough to take the records.

changes.heading: Changes to these terms
changes.body: These will change as the product does, and as the open questions on the privacy page close. Material changes get told to shops directly rather than re-dated here without notice.

percentArm.paymentsNote3: No row carries a DiveDay fee. DiveDay’s {percent} is billed to you once a month, on an invoice of its own.
percentArm.paymentsFaq1A: Yes. The fee is {percent} of money recorded as received in DiveDay{hasBase, select, yes {, plus {base} a month} other {}}, billed monthly. Cash and external payments count too. Separately recorded tips, tax and pass-through fees are excluded. Nothing is added to your guest’s price. Stripe charges its own card fees.

onlineBooking.name: Online booking
onlineBooking.summary: Divers book and pay for seats from your schedule, and a boat stops selling once it’s full.
onlineBooking.metaDescription: Divers book their own seats at any hour, with rental gear, a nitrox request and payment in one pass, after reading the certification the trip needs. Seats come off the boat’s capacity, so a trip can’t be oversold.
onlineBooking.title: Divers book while you’re out on the water
onlineBooking.lede: Divers see the trip’s certification requirements before booking. Your schedule takes their booking, rental gear, nitrox request and payment, and stops selling when the departure is full.
onlineBooking.screenLabel: A departure’s booking panel as a diver sees it: the certification the trip asks for, seats left, divers, rental gear and nitrox, and the total.
onlineBooking.note1: The certification the trip asks for sits above the button, where a diver reads it before paying.
onlineBooking.note2: Seats left is the boat’s capacity less every seat sold or held, counted again as the booking saves.
onlineBooking.note3: Nitrox is priced per dive, and a diver who asks without a checked nitrox card is planned on air.
onlineBooking.step1Title: Put the schedule where divers look
onlineBooking.step1Body: Your departures have their own DiveDay page, and a Book Now button or the calendar pastes onto the site you already have.
onlineBooking.step2Body: They choose how many divers, rental gear and nitrox, then pay in full or leave a deposit. A party organizer receives a claim link for each person they named.
onlineBooking.step3Title: The booking lands on the departure
onlineBooking.step3Body: A confirmation goes to the diver, with the waiver link in its own email when the trip needs one. The seat appears on the departure’s Divers tab with whatever is still missing.
onlineBooking.faq1Q: Can divers book from my own website?
onlineBooking.faq1A: Yes. Paste a Book Now button, a booking window or the calendar onto the site you have. WordPress, Squarespace and Wix take the same code.
onlineBooking.faq2Q: What happens when a departure fills up?
onlineBooking.faq2A: It stops selling seats and offers its wait list instead. When a seat frees up, staff invite whoever on it fits, by email, in one tap.
onlineBooking.faq3A: Yes. One booking covers up to twenty divers, and the organizer gets a claim link for each person they named, who then fills in their own details and waiver.
onlineBooking.closeTitle: Book a seat on the demo shop’s schedule
onlineBooking.demoPlace: the shop’s schedule, as a diver

website.name: Your website
website.summary: A booking page in your shop’s colors, and booking buttons for the site you already have.
website.metaTitle: Dive shop website and booking page
website.metaDescription: A booking page in your shop’s color, typeface and photos, plus a Book Now button, calendar and trip grid for WordPress, Squarespace or Wix.
website.title: Divers book on a page in your shop’s colors, rated only by divers who dived with you
website.lede: Your booking page wears your color, typeface and photos, and its buttons paste onto the site you run. Need help with a new website? Reach out to discuss what you have in mind.
website.screenLabel: A shop’s public booking page: the shop’s name and rating, the next boat with space, and the week’s departures.
website.note1: The shop’s color, the typeface on its name and “Since 1987” are set once, in Settings.
website.note2: The next boat with space comes first, for the diver who wants to go out tomorrow.
website.note3: The stars count only reviews written after a trip with you.
website.step1Body: Choose a color, a typeface and a cover photo, then add your agency badges and photos of the shop.
website.step2Body: Copy one code for a Book Now button, a booking window, the calendar, a trip grid, one departure or your courses. It picks up your site’s color and typeface.
website.step3Title: Let search engines read the trips
website.step3Body: Each trip, course and dive site page carries its price, open seats and rating in the form search engines read, and you decide whether the shop is listed.
website.faq1Q: I don’t have a website. Can you make one?
website.faq1A: Reach out to discuss what you need with a person at DiveDay. If you already have a site, you can add our booking buttons, calendar and trip grid yourself.
website.faq2Q: Will the booking button work on WordPress, Squarespace and Wix?
website.faq2A: Yes. It’s one code for all three, and the embed page in Settings shows the extra line each one needs.
website.faq3Q: Can divers read it in Spanish?
website.faq3A: Yes. Your public pages switch between English and Spanish from the header, and a diver’s own links open in the language they chose.
website.closeTitle: Look around a booking page made with DiveDay
website.demoPlace: the shop’s booking page, as a diver

waivers.name: Waivers and medical forms
waivers.summary: Releases and the diver medical form signed from home, sealed, and checked before anyone boards.
waivers.metaTitle: Online dive waivers and medical forms
waivers.metaDescription: Divers sign your release and the 2026 diver medical questionnaire from home. An answer that refers the diver to a doctor holds them until staff record a physician’s clearance.
waivers.title: Waivers and medical forms come back signed before the diver walks in
waivers.lede: Divers sign at home from the link emailed when they book, and an answer that refers them to a doctor keeps them off the boat until a physician’s clearance is on file.
waivers.screenLabel: The waiver page on a diver’s phone: the release, the medical questions and the typed signature.
waivers.note1: The link stays open for seven days and saves each answer as the diver goes.
waivers.note2: The signature is typed, and the signed record is sealed so a later change to it can be detected.
waivers.note3: A yes that needs a doctor tells the diver at once, and holds them until staff record the sign-off.
waivers.step1Body: Put your release text in Settings. Each change becomes a new version, and every signed copy keeps the version it was signed against.
waivers.step2Body: The link goes out by email the moment they book, unless a release they signed is still current. The diver reads the release, answers the medical questions and types their name.
waivers.step3Title: The desk sees who hasn’t signed
waivers.step3Body: Unsigned releases are listed on the staff home screen by boat, with the diver’s name when there’s only one, and one tap sends every waiver not yet sent for a departure.
waivers.faq1Q: What if a diver turns up without signing?
waivers.faq1A: Send the link again from their row, or record a release they signed on paper, once you’ve checked that none of their medical answers needs a physician.
waivers.faq2A: A release signed under 18 asks a parent or guardian to sign too, and boarding waits for both. A diver counts as under 18 when the date of birth on their record says so or, with no date on file, when whoever booked them ticked “Under 18”.
waivers.faq3Q: What about waivers divers already signed with my old system?
waivers.faq3A: If your old system’s export marks a diver’s waiver as accepted, the importer brings it across, dated and marked imported, and trusts the medical clearance your old system recorded. The diver isn’t asked to sign again while it’s current.
waivers.closeTitle: See the release editor and every signed copy
waivers.demoPlace: the release and every signed copy, as the owner

certifications.name: Certification checks
certifications.summary: Each diver is Ready or Blocked for each departure, with the missing card, form or payment named.
certifications.metaTitle: Dive certification checks for every departure
certifications.metaDescription: DiveDay checks each diver’s cards against what the departure and its dive sites ask for, such as deep, wreck, night or nitrox, and names what is missing days before the boat leaves.
certifications.title: Know who can board days before the boat leaves, and what the others are missing
certifications.lede: DiveDay checks each diver against the level and the Deep, Wreck or nitrox card the departure and its sites ask for, plus the waiver, medical form and payment it requires, and names what’s missing.
certifications.screenLabel: Today in DiveDay: a departure’s readiness bar, then the Needs you list with the reason beside each name.
certifications.note1: The bar is the departure’s seats: green for ready divers, red for blocked ones, the rest still open.
certifications.note2: A card a diver entered that nobody has checked keeps them blocked until someone on staff does.
certifications.note3: Each row says what is in the way and the boat it’s for, and names the diver when they’re the only one.
certifications.step1Body: Pick the level a departure needs and any Deep, Wreck, Night or Drysuit card, on the departure or on its sites. A departure can also require a nitrox card.
certifications.step2Title: Cards come in with the diver
certifications.step2Body: Divers add their agency, level and number from their trip link after they book, and staff mark a card certified once they’ve checked it with the agency.
certifications.step3Title: Desk and dock read the same answer
certifications.step3Body: Each diver reads Ready or Blocked everywhere they appear, and at the dock the roll call won’t mark a diver aboard until they’re cleared.
certifications.faq1Q: Can I bring my divers’ cards over from my current system?
certifications.faq1A: Yes. The importer brings certification records across from your old system’s export. Level cards count as they stood there, marked imported, and a nitrox or specialty card waits until a staff member confirms it.
certifications.faq2Q: What about a diver halfway through a course?
certifications.faq2A: If they’re booked on a course that brings them to the level and finishes before the dive, the seat can be sold, and boarding waits for the new card.
certifications.faq3Q: Does nitrox need its own card?
certifications.faq3A: Yes, a nitrox card on file. A request is checked against it every time the roster is read, and a diver without a checked card is planned on air. RAID and GUE teach nitrox inside the level card, so staff record that card’s number as the nitrox card.
certifications.closeTitle: See which demo divers are blocked, and why
certifications.demoPlace: the day’s boats and what each diver still needs, as the owner

messages.name: Messages to divers
messages.summary: Confirmations, a reminder a week out, a brief the day before and the recap go out on their own, and email replies land in one inbox.
messages.metaTitle: Automatic booking reminders and dive trip messages
messages.metaDescription: Confirmation and waiver emails, a reminder a week out, a brief the day before with the dock time, and a recap after the dive. Divers’ email replies land in one inbox.
messages.title: The day before, each diver gets the dock time and a list of what’s still theirs to do
messages.lede: Confirmations, a reminder a week out and a brief the day before go out by email with a text alongside, and a failed email shows up for your staff with a Resend button.
messages.screenLabel: The night-before page on a diver’s phone: the dock time, waiver and certification done, and gear still to fill in.
messages.note1: The dock time opens the page, because it’s the line a diver checks first thing in the morning.
messages.note2: “Your turn” marks what is still the diver’s to do, here their gear.
messages.note3: The reminder email carries the same list, with a link back to this page.
messages.step1Title: From booking to the week before
messages.step1Body: The confirmation goes out at booking, and the waiver link follows in its own email when the trip needs one. A week before, a reminder lists anything the diver still has to do, by email with a text alongside.
messages.step2Body: The second reminder is a brief: the dock time, the conditions, what to bring and who to text, linked to the diver’s own trip page.
messages.step3Body: The recap shows the sites, a note from the crew and the photos, and asks how the day went.
messages.faq1Q: Can a diver reply to a reminder?
messages.faq1A: Yes. A reply to one of your emails lands in your Inbox and on the diver’s record, where staff can answer it by email.
messages.faq2Q: Can the texts come from our own WhatsApp number?
messages.faq2A: Yes. Connect the shop’s WhatsApp number in Settings, and reminder and recap texts go out from that number. Replies on WhatsApp land in your Inbox.
messages.faq3Q: Can I stop a send I tapped by mistake?
messages.faq3A: Waiver links for a whole departure, a last-minute deal and a wait-list invite each wait eight seconds with an Undo button before they go.
messages.closeTitle: Read the replies waiting in the demo Inbox
messages.demoPlace: the shop’s Inbox, as the owner

checkIn.name: Check-in
checkIn.summary: One tap per diver at the counter, a lookup for anyone unsure of their boat, and walk-ins added on the spot.
checkIn.metaTitle: Dive shop check-in for the morning rush
checkIn.metaDescription: Check divers in with one tap on the departure’s own list. Anyone not ready shows what’s missing instead of the tap, and walk-ins can fill in their own details from the code on your counter before you seat them.
checkIn.title: The morning rush is one tap per diver
checkIn.lede: Arrivals open on the departure’s Divers tab, with a count of who’s here, a Check in tap beside each diver who’s ready, and what’s missing beside anyone who isn’t.
checkIn.screenLabel: A departure’s Divers tab during arrivals: the count of divers here, a checked-in diver, a Check in tap, and a held seat asking whether it’s the same person.
checkIn.note1: The count is divers here against divers booked, and it moves only when a tap lands.
checkIn.note2: A held seat asks Same person or Different person, so paperwork stays with the diver it names.
checkIn.note3: A diver who isn’t ready has no Check in tap, and their row carries the fix instead.
checkIn.step1Body: In the hours around a departure, its Divers tab shows the count and a Check in tap beside every diver who’s ready, each with an undo.
checkIn.step2Title: Fix what’s missing at the desk
checkIn.step2Body: A blocked diver’s row carries its own fix: send the waiver, record a paper release, take the payment or confirm who they are.
checkIn.step3Body: Add a walk-in from the tab, or let them fill in their details on their own phone from the code on your counter, then seat them. Once the boat’s time passes, Not here? frees the seat and shows who is waiting for it.
checkIn.faq1Q: What if a diver can’t remember which boat they’re on?
checkIn.faq1A: Search by name, phone or email from DiveDay’s opening screen, or scan the code on their confirmation. It looks across every departure from six hours ago to a day and a half ahead.
checkIn.faq2Q: Can a walk-in fill in their own details?
checkIn.faq2A: Yes. The code on your counter card opens a form on their phone for their name, contact details, certification and rental sizes, and a walk-in is sent the release, by text if they gave a phone number and no email. Then seat them from the Divers tab.
checkIn.faq3Q: What happens when someone doesn’t show?
checkIn.faq3A: Once the boat’s time has passed, mark them Not here. Their seat opens, the wait list shows beside it, and nothing is charged or refunded by that tap.
checkIn.closeTitle: Check in the divers on the next demo boat
checkIn.demoPlace: the day’s departures, as the owner

boatManifest.name: Boat manifest and roll call
boatManifest.summary: Every diver and crew member called by name, before the boat leaves and after every dive, on a phone that works out of signal range.
boatManifest.metaTitle: Dive boat manifest and roll call
boatManifest.metaDescription: The crew calls every diver and crew member by name before departure and after every dive, on a phone that keeps the manifest with no signal. A tap made out of range is sent once the phone has signal again.
boatManifest.title: Call every diver back aboard by name after every dive, with or without a signal
boatManifest.lede: Any crew phone that opens DiveDay with signal saves the next two days’ manifests, and roll calls taken out of range join the live record when the phone reconnects.
boatManifest.screenLabel: The captain’s roll call at the dock: the head count, the checkpoint, and a circle to tap on each name.
boatManifest.note1: Every diver is counted aboard by a tap on their own name, so no one is marked present in bulk.
boatManifest.note2: Each row opens the diver’s sheet: contact, gear, medical, and why a blocked diver can’t board.
boatManifest.note3: An untapped circle stays open, so a missed tap never reads as aboard.
boatManifest.step1Body: Opening DiveDay with signal saves the next two days’ manifests to the phone, divers and crew both.
boatManifest.step2Title: Call the roll at every checkpoint
boatManifest.step2Body: Before departure and after each dive, the crew taps each name aboard or not aboard, crew included.
boatManifest.step3Title: It squares up back in range
boatManifest.step3Body: Taps made with no signal are labeled that way until the phone reconnects. A tap the live record has moved past comes back marked refused rather than written over.
boatManifest.faq1Q: What if two crew phones are counting at once?
boatManifest.faq1A: With signal, both see the same roll call as it changes, and a tap the record has already moved past is refused rather than written over. Out of range, each phone sees only its own taps until it reconnects, so call each checkpoint on one phone.
boatManifest.faq2A: Yes. The trip packet prints the dive plan, the manifest with its roll call and the emergency card you fill in (your nearest chamber, DAN, the coast guard), and the packing list.
boatManifest.faq3Q: What does a diver see while we’re out?
boatManifest.faq3A: Their own trip link shows a line about the boat each time the crew taps a stage: boarding, out at the site, on the surface, heading in and back at the dock.
boatManifest.closeTitle: Call the roll on the demo boat as its captain
boatManifest.demoPlace: the day’s boats, as the captain

diveSites.name: Dive sites and briefings
diveSites.summary: Each site’s route, landmarks and marine life written once, and shown to every diver on a boat that goes there.
diveSites.metaTitle: Dive site briefings for your divers
diveSites.metaDescription: Write each dive site once: depth, route, landmarks with photos and what lives there. Every diver booked on a boat to that site reads the briefing before they come.
diveSites.title: Write each dive site once
diveSites.lede: Divers read the route, landmarks and recent sightings before they come. Each site’s depth, terrain map, photos and species stay together on their trip page.
diveSites.screenLabel: A dive site briefing as divers read it before the trip: the site, its depth and time in the water, the route, and what has been seen there this month.
diveSites.note1: Depth is the site’s own, in your shop’s units, and time in the water is your usual for that dive.
diveSites.note2: The route starts at a hollow circle and finishes at a filled one, so a diver reads which way the dive swims.
diveSites.note3: Seen here this month comes from what your crew logged after their dives.
diveSites.step1Body: Add the depth and difficulty, draw the route on the map, add landmarks with their photos, and pick species from the field guide.
diveSites.step2Body: Give a departure up to four dives, each with its site, and the briefings line up in dive order with your usual time in the water and on the surface between dives.
diveSites.step3Body: The briefing sits on each booked diver’s trip page, and every site has a public page of its own for divers searching for the reef.
diveSites.faq1Q: Do I have to write every site from scratch?
diveSites.faq1A: If you dive Florida, DiveDay has 34 sites written up, from the Keys to the springs, ready to copy and edit. Anywhere else, you write your own.
diveSites.faq2Q: Can a site require a certification?
diveSites.faq2A: Yes. A site can require a level and a specialty card such as Deep or Wreck, and every departure going there asks for it.
diveSites.faq3Q: Is the field guide in Spanish too?
diveSites.faq3A: Yes. DiveDay writes the descriptions of its 148 Caribbean and Florida species in English and Spanish.
diveSites.closeTitle: Browse the demo shop’s dive sites
diveSites.demoPlace: the shop’s dive sites, as the owner

rentalGear.name: Rental gear
rentalGear.summary: Every unit on your wall with its size and service due, reserved for one diver at a time, and your customers’ own gear on the bench.
rentalGear.metaTitle: Dive gear rental and service tracking
rentalGear.metaDescription: Track every BCD, regulator, wetsuit and cylinder by tag, size and service date. Staff reserve a unit to one booking, and the register won’t give it to a second diver on the same dates.
rentalGear.title: Know which wetsuit is on which diver, and which regulator is due for service
rentalGear.lede: List your own units by tag, size and serial, reserve one to a booking from the departure’s Gear tab, and see each regulator, cylinder and BCD’s next service date. When a customer brings their own regulator in, it goes on the bench as a work order, and they hear when it’s ready.
rentalGear.screenLabel: The gear register: units by kind with their counts, then each unit’s tag, model, size and status.
rentalGear.note1: The chips count units of each kind, so a short shelf shows before the morning.
rentalGear.note2: A reserved unit names its diver, and the register won’t give it to anyone else.
rentalGear.note3: Service due is a warning on the row, and whether the unit goes out is your call.
rentalGear.step1Body: Add units by hand or from a spreadsheet, with tag, kind, size, serial and model.
rentalGear.step2Title: Divers give their sizes after booking
rentalGear.step2Body: The Gear tab turns those sizes into a list to pull and lists free units, exact size first.
rentalGear.step3Body: Stamp a unit out and back, print the diver’s rental slip, and see overdue returns and service coming due on the day’s to-do list. Repairs run on work orders: the customer is told when theirs is ready, and gets the bill by email.
rentalGear.faq1Q: Which service checks can it track?
rentalGear.faq1A: Annual service, hydrostatic test, visual inspection and oxygen cleaning, each with its due date, plus a dive count where the manufacturer sets one.
rentalGear.faq2Q: What if two divers want the same unit?
rentalGear.faq2A: Staff reserve a unit to one booking, and the register refuses to give it to another diver whose dates overlap.
rentalGear.faq3Q: Do I have to tag every unit to rent gear?
rentalGear.faq3A: No. Divers can rent gear and give their sizes with no register at all. The register is there for when you want to track units.
rentalGear.closeTitle: Look through the demo fleet, unit by unit
rentalGear.demoPlace: the gear register, as the owner

schedule.name: Schedule and crew
schedule.summary: Build the season’s departures, repeat the regular ones, and see which boat still needs crew.
schedule.metaTitle: Dive trip scheduling and crew planning
schedule.metaDescription: Add, move and copy departures in place, repeat a weekly trip with no end date, and put crew on each boat. The crew view shows which departure is uncovered.
schedule.title: Regular trips repeat on their own, and a boat with no crew yet says so on the week’s board
schedule.lede: When you call off a boat for weather, one confirmed tap cancels it, emails every diver the departures they qualify for, and refunds their online card payments.
schedule.screenLabel: The week’s schedule: departures by day with their times, crew and seats filled, and an Add button on each day.
schedule.note1: Each row shows how many of the boat’s seats are filled, so a thin departure stands out early.
schedule.note2: “Crew: nobody yet” marks a boat no one is assigned to, on the same row as its seats.
schedule.note3: Add sits on every day, so a new departure starts on the date you’re looking at.
schedule.step1Body: Add a departure on its day, then move, copy or remove it in place. A course session or a multi-day trip is one departure with one roster.
schedule.step2Body: Set a trip to run every Saturday, on Mondays and Thursdays, or daily. The series rolls forward on its own and edits as one.
schedule.step3Body: Assign captains, instructors and divemasters, with an instructor on every course session. The same person on two boats at once is refused, and a later change that overlaps them is flagged.
schedule.faq1Q: What if a boat fills and divers keep asking?
schedule.faq1A: A full departure with a long wait list suggests adding another boat or a second departure, and when someone cancels, staff invite whoever on the list fits.
schedule.faq2Q: Can staff see their trips in their own calendar?
schedule.faq2A: Yes. Each staffer can subscribe to departures in Google, Apple or Outlook calendar.
schedule.faq3Q: What if a trip doesn’t get enough divers?
schedule.faq3A: Give it a minimum and a time to decide by. If the minimum isn’t met by then, the departure cancels itself, emails each diver on it and refunds their card payments.
schedule.closeTitle: Add a departure to the demo week
schedule.demoPlace: the week’s schedule, as the owner

courses.name: Courses
courses.summary: Course pages in the order you teach them, with dates divers can book and an instructor on every session.
courses.metaDescription: Course pages with price, prerequisites, a day-by-day plan and bookable dates, started from PADI, SSI or SDI content. PADI Open Water sessions and try dives stop selling at their ratio, and whoever books online confirms each diver meets the course’s minimum age.
courses.title: Divers book course dates from your own site
courses.lede: Make a PADI, SSI or SDI course yours with your price, prerequisites, plan and photos. A PADI Open Water session stops selling at its instructor ratio.
courses.screenLabel: A public course page: the agency, the course name and price, the plan by day, and an upcoming date to book.
courses.note1: The agency sits above the title, so a diver comparing shops knows which card they’ll get.
courses.note2: The plan by day is the shop’s own, edited from the catalog it started with.
courses.note3: Each upcoming date books like a departure, with its own seats.
courses.step1Body: Copy in courses from PADI, SSI or SDI, then edit the price, the plan and the photos into your own.
courses.step2Body: Each date is a departure with an instructor on it. A PADI Open Water session sells up to PADI’s ratio, with room added for each assistant, and a try dive up to two divers per instructor.
courses.step3Body: Divers pick a date on the course page, and a course that certifies them first lets them book the dive that needs the new card.
courses.faq1Q: Can a diver ask for a date that isn’t listed?
courses.faq1A: Yes. The course page takes a date request, and it lands in your Inbox grouped by day.
courses.faq2Q: Which ratios does it hold sessions to?
courses.faq2A: PADI Open Water allows eight students per instructor, two more for each divemaster or assistant instructor, and never more than twelve. DiveDay holds every try dive to two divers per instructor, whatever the agency, and an assistant adds no room. Other courses are limited by the departure’s seats.
courses.faq3A: Yes. Whoever books online confirms every diver meets the course’s minimum age, and once a diver’s date of birth is on their record, it’s checked on the day the course runs and an under-age diver can’t board. DiveDay doesn’t ask divers for a date of birth, so confirm ages at the desk.
courses.closeTitle: See the demo catalog and its course dates
courses.demoPlace: the course catalog, as the owner

payments.name: Payments
payments.summary: Cards, deposits and refunds through your own Stripe account, with each day’s orders on one ledger.
payments.metaTitle: Dive shop payments, deposits and refunds
payments.metaDescription: Take card payments and deposits at booking through your own Stripe account. Refunds go out by themselves when you call a blow-out or too few divers cancels a boat.
payments.title: Divers pay when they book, and the money lands in your own Stripe account
payments.lede: Take the full price or a deposit at booking, invoice anything else from the desk, and when a boat is canceled, every online card payment on it refunds by itself.
payments.screenLabel: The Orders page: one day’s orders with the count and subtotal, and each order’s status.
payments.note1: Orders file by day with the day’s count and subtotal, the way the till is counted at close.
payments.note2: Open means the order still has money owed on it.
payments.note3: DiveDay’s software fee is billed monthly, separately from each guest’s payment.
payments.step1Body: Payouts, disputes and history stay in the shop’s own Stripe account.
payments.step2Body: Charge in full or take a deposit, add sales tax or VAT through Stripe, and nudge a diver who reserved but never finished paying.
payments.step3Body: Every order sits on its day’s ledger, and the monthly report shows revenue, bookings and seat fill per trip.
payments.faq1Q: Do you take a percentage of bookings?
payments.faq1A: No. DiveDay is one flat monthly price. Stripe charges its own card fees in your Stripe account.
payments.faq2Q: What happens when a diver cancels?
payments.faq2A: Inside the free-cancellation window you set, an online card payment is refunded by itself. Past the window, a refund is yours to decide.
payments.faq3Q: Does it work with my accounting?
payments.faq3A: Paid and refunded orders post to QuickBooks as receipts, and the report downloads as a spreadsheet.
payments.closeTitle: Look over a day of demo orders
payments.demoPlace: the day’s orders, as the owner
